title: Analysis of perceived information gaps in inpatient hospital care as a basis for the development of an AI-based digital assistance system
summary:
Background:
In hospitals, patients often do not receive or fully understand all the information they need for their treatment and stay. This can lead to uncertainty and dissatisfaction. At the same time, hospital staff face the challenge of providing complete and understandable information in everyday clinical practice.

Research question:
The aim of the study is to investigate which information gaps exist from the perspective of patients and hospital staff and at which points during the hospital stay these occur most frequently.

Methods:
Patients and hospital staff are invited to participate in an anonymous survey. In addition, interviews are conducted with selected participants to gain a deeper understanding of the results. Participation is voluntary.
conditions: Perceived information gaps in inpatient hospital care

interventions.name:
In this non-interventional study, patients and hospital staff are surveyed regarding perceived information gaps in the inpatient care process.

Data collection is conducted in two stages:
(1) standardized, anonymous online questionnaires (EvaSys) to quantitatively assess perceived information gap

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients aged 18 years or older with a current or recent inpatient hospital stay, as well as hospital staff. Sufficient German language skills to complete the questionnaire or participate in interviews. Ability to provide informed consent and voluntary participation.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals under 18 years of age. Lack of ability to provide informed consent. Insufficient German language skills to participate in the survey or interviews.
